raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`_fwd_kernel` and `_fwd_kernel_unified` in `extend_attention.py` load a KV slot from `kv_indices` and multiply it by the KV buffer stride in the index dtype. With int32 `kv_indices` the product wraps once `slot >= 2^31 / stride`, which is 2,097,152 tokens for 8 KV heads x 128 head dim. The kernel then faults or, when the wrapped address is mapped, silently reads the wrong KV.

The aiter backend's CUDA-graph `cuda_graph_kv_indices` is int32 and is used as-is by the legacy target-verify path (NGRAM, EAGLE with topk > 1), so a long-running aiter server whose KV pool exceeds that size eventually crashes in `_fwd_kernel`. Spec-decode `kv_indices` built in `eagle_info.py` / `ngram_info.py` are also int32. The triton backend's own buffers are int64 and are not affected.

## Modifications

- `extend_attention.py`: cast the loaded slot to int64 before the address math in `_fwd_kernel` and `_fwd_kernel_unified`. This covers the `PAGE_SIZE == 1` and paged branches and any caller dtype.
- `test_triton_attention_kernels.py`: add `test_extend_attention_int32_kv_indices_above_2g`, which runs both kernels with int32 slots above `2^31 / stride` against the same data at low slots. The slots sit just below `2^32 / stride` so a wrapped offset reads zero rows in front of the buffer rather than faulting (~8.6 GB). On main both subtests fail (max abs diff 1.09 / 1.04); with this PR they pass.

## Accuracy Tests

Only addressing changes: for slots below 2^31 / stride the int64 cast leaves every offset unchanged, so outputs are unchanged.

MI355X (gfx950), torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, triton 3.8.0, aiter `285579b62`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, CUDA graphs on, `amd/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-FP8-KV` with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --speculative-algorithm NGRAM`; the KV pool is 3,503,271 tokens. Every fault below is a `Memory Fault` in `_fwd_kernel` with grid `[24576, 32, 1]`:

- main `7fe5b127e4`, GSM8K (1319 questions, `--max-tokens 4096`): faults between questions 430 and 485 in three runs, when cumulative allocated slots reach about 2.1M.
- With the KV-scale fix (#47030) applied, `bench_serving` random 512 in / 4096 out, 600 prompts, concurrency 48: faults after 265 s. The same run on the triton backend completes.
- This PR, the same `bench_serving` run on aiter: all 600 requests complete (2.46M output tokens, 1792 s) without a fault.

Unit tests: `test_triton_attention_kernels.py` and `test_gemma4_unified_swa_virtual_ids.py` pass (18 tests, with `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI_AMD=1`).

MI325X (gfx942), torch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0, aiter `285579b62`, main `cb55d77d37` with this patch: the new test fails on main and passes here (the two gfx950-only tests skip). NVIDIA is not tested.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

`extend_attention_fwd`, 32 Q heads, 8 KV heads, head dim 128, bf16 KV, MI355X, median of 7 x 50 calls:

| Shape | int32 indices, main | int32 indices, this PR |
|---|---|---|
| verify bs 48, prefix 1024, extend 12, custom mask | 333.4 us | 332.2 us |
| verify bs 8, prefix 4096, extend 8, custom mask | 207.2 us | 206.2 us |
| prefill bs 4, prefix 2048, extend 512 | 231.9 us | 232.9 us |
| prefill bs 1, prefix 8192, extend 2048 | 873.2 us | 873.0 us |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -581,6 +581,9 @@ def _fwd_kernel(
                     mask=mask_n,
                     other=0,
                 )
+            # Callers may pass int32 kv_indices; slot * stride overflows int32
+            # once slot >= 2^31 / stride (2M tokens at 8 heads x 128 dim).
+            offs_kv_loc = offs_kv_loc.to(tl.int64)
 
             # Page-aware KV address math. At PAGE_SIZE==1
             # (legacy / non-shared / shared-at-ps=1), Triton specializes
@@ -1364,7 +1367,7 @@ def _fwd_kernel_unified(
                 kv_indices + cur_seq_kv_start_idx + start_n + offs_n,
                 mask=mask_n,
                 other=0,
-            )
+            ).to(tl.int64)
 
             # Page-aware KV address math (see _fwd_kernel_stage1).
             if PAGE_SIZE == 1:

@@ -682,6 +682,84 @@ def _test_context_attention_once(self, head_dim, is_causal):
             self.assertTrue(cos_sim.item() > 1 - (1e-5))
             self.assertTrue(torch.allclose(o[start:end], o_torch, atol=1e-2))
 
+    def test_extend_attention_int32_kv_indices_above_2g(self):
+        """Regression for int32 KV offset overflow in the extend kernels.
+
+        With int32 kv_indices, slot * stride wraps once slot >= 2**31 / stride.
+        Slots sit just below 2**32 / stride so a wrapped offset lands on the
+        zero rows in front of the buffer and shows up as a mismatch, not a
+        fault. Needs ~8.6 GB.
+        """
+        device = get_device()
+        dtype = torch.bfloat16
+        B, P, E, H_Q, D = 2, 64, 16, 8, 128
+        pad, num_slots = 256, 2**32 // D
+        big = torch.zeros(pad + num_slots, 1, D, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+        kv_buffer = big[pad:]
+
+        q = torch.randn(B * E, H_Q, D, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+        kv = torch.randn(B, P + E, 1, D, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+        k_ext = kv[:, P:].reshape(B * E, 1, D)
+        slots = torch.arange(B * (P + E), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        high_slots = slots + (num_slots - pad)
+        kv_buffer[high_slots.long()] = kv.flatten(0, 1)
+        ref_buffer = kv.flatten(0, 1)
+
+        qo_indptr = torch.arange(0, (B + 1) * E, E, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        prefix_indptr = torch.arange(
+            0, (B + 1) * P, P, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+        )
+        unified_indptr = torch.arange(
+            0, (B + 1) * (P + E), P + E, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+        )
+        prefix_lens = torch.full((B,), P, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+
+        def run(buf, idx, unified):
+            o = torch.empty_like(q)
+            if unified:
+                extend_attention_fwd_unified(
+                    q,
+                    o,
+                    buf,
+                    buf,
+                    1.0,
+                    1.0,
+                    qo_indptr,
+                    unified_indptr,
+                    idx,
+                    prefix_lens,
+                    max_len_extend=E,
+                )
+            else:
+                prefix_idx = idx.view(B, P + E)[:, :P].flatten()
+                extend_attention_fwd(
+                    q,
+                    k_ext,
+                    k_ext,
+                    o,
+                    buf,
+                    buf,
+                    qo_indptr,
+                    prefix_indptr,
+                    prefix_idx,
+                    None,
+                    True,
+                    None,
+                    E,
+                    1.0,
+                    1.0,
+                )
+            return o
+
+        for unified in (False, True):
+            with self.subTest(unified=unified):
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    run(kv_buffer, high_slots, unified),
+                    run(ref_buffer, slots, unified),
+                    atol=1e-2,
+                    rtol=1e-2,
+                )
+
     def test_context_attention(self):
         head_dim = [128, 96, 80, 13]
